newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Sen. Lott calls for budget framework soon.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Sen. Lott calls for budget framework soon.

text.p: Senate Majority Leader Trent Lott said on Thursday that budget negotiations with the White House must produce a "framework" for a budget agreement by the week's end or he will push to work out a final plan with conservative Democrats.

"I really think we have got to have a conceptual agreement by this week or we are going to have to move on," the Mississippi Republican said. He spoke with President Clinton by telephone Wednesday on the budget, but provided few details beyond their agreement that the issue needs to be concluded.
"We have been going on this dance around the bush for three months and we need to come to some conclusions," Lott told reporters.

In order for a budget agreement to pass the Senate with Democratic support, Lott said the next step would be to work with conservative Democrats. "We would move over into working with them much more aggressively," absent a deal with the White House, he said.

White House and congressional negotiators are to resume talks at 2:45 p.m. EDT (1630 GMT). After this session they will take a few days to assess progress and decide whether budget work should continue.
